replacement_spec.body: A transfer function is the representation of a linear time-invariant system as the ratio of the transform of its output to the transform of its input with zero initial conditions: H(s) = Y(s)/X(s) in the Laplace domain for continuous-time systems, H(z) = Y(z)/X(z) in the Z domain for discrete-time systems. Parameters: (1) the LTI system whose input-output relation is mapped, (2) the complex domain of the representation (s or z), (3) the numerator and denominator polynomials, whose roots place the system's zeros and poles. The function persists through mathematical notation in control and signal-processing textbooks, engineering standards, and reproducible implementations; engineers use it to analyze stability, predict frequency response, and design controllers and filters. [formal: functio transferens | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
